scope_subject: Project Checks — Backend (Java 21 / Spring Boot 3) — Phase 2

article_iv_gate.description: Every entry in this file traces to a PRD or ARCH section. No invented requirements. @pm attests.

complexity_signals: 9 external integrations (CSI, ITRS, Splunk, Grafana, AppDynamics, OIDC, Vault, SMTP, Selenium Grid, S3)
Regulated domain (Citibank): SSO + RBAC + secrets vault mandatory
Browser automation infrastructure (video recording, S3 streaming)
Polymorphic check model with 7 check types via JSONB

functional.title: Associate every check with a registered CSI
functional.description: All checks MUST reference a CSI ID that exists in csi_systems. CSI is the primary organizing principle for catalog, dashboards, and reports.

functional.title: Expose CSI catalog via REST API
functional.description: Backend exposes GET /csi, GET /csi/{id}, GET /csi/{id}/checks for directory and drill-down.

functional.title: Aggregate health metrics per CSI
functional.description: GET /csi/{id}/metrics returns real-time passing/failing/warning counts and health percentage, backed by the csi_metrics_current materialized view.

functional.title: Support 7 polymorphic check types
functional.description: Supported types: HTTP, TCP, SPLUNK, GRAFANA, ITRS, APPDYNAMICS, UI_TEST. Type-specific configuration stored in JSONB column.

functional.title: Check CRUD operations via REST
functional.description: GET /checks (list + filters), POST /checks, GET /checks/{id}, PUT /checks/{id}, DELETE /checks/{id} (soft delete via deleted_at).

functional.title: On-demand check execution with async response
functional.description: POST /checks/{id}/execute returns 202 Accepted with execution ID immediately; work runs on virtual-thread executor; result persisted to execution_results.

functional.title: HTTP(S) endpoint check
functional.description: Full configurable: method (GET/POST/...), headers, body, expected status code validation, TLS verification.

functional.title: TCP port check
functional.description: Host/port connectivity validation with configurable timeout.

functional.title: Splunk SPL query check
functional.description: Execute complex SPL queries against Splunk and validate result-count thresholds.

functional.title: Grafana metric threshold check
functional.description: Dashboard/panel metric monitoring with configurable operator (>, <, =, !=, …) and threshold.

functional.title: ITRS Geneos sampler status check
functional.description: Real-time sampler state monitoring with expected-value comparison.

functional.title: AppDynamics health rule violation check
functional.description: Monitors AppDynamics application health rules and APM alerts.

functional.title: Persist execution history
functional.description: Every execution records status, started_at, ended_at, duration_ms, output, error_message in execution_results (partitioned monthly).

functional.title: Auto-propagate execution result to parent check status
functional.description: DB trigger update_check_on_execution cascades the latest execution status into checks.status + last_execution_at.

functional.title: Deep link to investigation URL on failure
functional.description: When a check fails, the response includes a URL to the underlying monitoring tool for drill-down.

functional.title: Cron-based scheduling
functional.description: Support standard cron expressions + human-readable frequency ('every_5_minutes'). Due checks auto-dispatched.

functional.title: Enable/disable schedules without deletion
functional.description: schedules.enabled boolean controls active dispatch; indexed for fast dispatcher scan.

functional.title: Timezone-aware scheduling
functional.description: schedules.timezone (default UTC) ensures cron resolution in the owner's timezone.

functional.title: Cluster-safe scheduling at scale
functional.description: Migrate from in-process @Scheduled to Quartz (JDBC-backed) once >1 replica is deployed.

functional.title: UI test definition CRUD (Checks Studio)
functional.description: Create, read, update, delete UI tests with plain-English steps, browser choice, viewport, timeout.

functional.title: Execute UI test via browser automation grid
functional.description: POST /studio/tests/{id}/run dispatches to Selenium Grid; results in ui_test_executions.

traces.ref: §4.4 M5 UI test execution via Selenium Grid client

functional.title: Video recording + S3 storage
functional.description: Every UI test run records a full-screen video, uploaded to S3; database stores URL pointer only.

traces.ref: §5 Object Storage for UI test videos

functional.title: Video streaming endpoint with step-synchronized timeline
functional.description: GET /studio/tests/{id}/video streams video; timeline marks mapped to test steps.

functional.title: Variable (<var NAME>) and secret (<secret ID>) interpolation
functional.description: Test steps support <var NAME> and <secret ID> tokens; resolved at execution time.

functional.title: Python code generation from test steps
functional.description: Export executable Python code equivalent to the plain-English steps.

functional.title: Report configuration CRUD
functional.description: Create, read, update, delete report definitions with template, schedule, recipients, sections.

functional.title: Live-preview endpoint for report builder
functional.description: POST /reports/{id}/preview returns rendered HTML preview without sending email.

traces.ref: §6 Live Preview is King UX philosophy

functional.title: Cross-CSI report composition
functional.description: A single report can aggregate checks from multiple CSIs (e.g., Trade Settled from CSI 12345 + Market Data from CSI 99887).

functional.title: Scheduled email delivery via SMTP relay
functional.description: Reports delivered via enterprise SMTP at configured cadence (daily/weekly/custom cron).

functional.title: Report execution audit trail
functional.description: Every delivery persists status, recipient_count, checks_included, generation_duration_ms, email_content, error_message.

functional.title: Send-now / ad-hoc trigger
functional.description: POST /reports/{id}/send triggers immediate out-of-cycle delivery.

functional.title: Authenticate every request via platform BFF session cookie
functional.description: Every authenticated endpoint resolves user identity via the platform BFF session (put_session cookie introspection against Core service at /api/v1/users/me, with forward-compat for Envoy-injected X-User-* headers). NOT direct COIN OIDC JWT validation — that is Core's exclusive concern. See spec.md §7.1 and put-platform-shell/docs/content/docs/architecture/authentication.md.

functional.title: RBAC by CSI ownership + permission-name checks
functional.description: Method-level @PreAuthorize with CsiOwnershipEvaluator uses the csi_ownership field of the resolved UserIdentity (from Core's /users/me response or X-User-Csi-Ownership gateway header). Endpoint-level permission-name checks (e.g., checks.bulk.execute) via @RequiresPermission annotation that delegates to Core's /api/v1/authz/check.

traces.ref: §7 RBAC based on user roles and application ownership

functional.title: User provisioning from Core-service identity
functional.description: On first-seen session, upsert into users(sso_id, name, email, department) using fields from the Core /api/v1/users/me response; subsequent auths update last_login. Local users table mirrors platform identity for FK integrity on created_by columns — it is NOT an alternate identity store.

functional.title: Resolve <secret ID> tokens from vault at execution time
functional.description: Check configurations contain <secret ID> references; backend resolves at execution time from enterprise vault. Secrets never persisted in plaintext, never returned in API responses.

functional.title: Tag checks and CSIs
functional.description: Tags are flexible metadata (name, category, color) associated with checks via check_tags and with CSIs via csi_tags.

functional.title: Multi-dimensional check list filtering
functional.description: GET /checks supports filters: csi_id, type, status, environment, tag, created_by, text search.

traces.ref: §5.3 Global search context with CSI, environment, and tag filtering
§7.1 checks indexes on csi_id, type, status

functional.title: Bulk operations on checks
functional.description: POST /checks/_bulk accepts up to 100 operations (delete, update, tag) in a single request with partial-failure semantics (207 Multi-Status). Authorized per-operation via CsiOwnershipEvaluator. Idempotency-Key honored at batch level.
functional.added_in_revision: Phase 5 (retroactive; was gap COMP-01 in critique.json)

traces.ref: §5.3 Bulk Operations: Multi-select and bulk actions for check management

non_functional.title: Simple check execution P50 < 100ms / P95 < 500ms / P99 < 1s
Complex check execution P50 < 5s / P95 < 10s / P99 < 30s
Structured JSON logs with correlation IDs
Execution result retention: 30d hot / 90d warm / 1y cold / hard delete
UI test video retention: 7d hot / 30d warm / hard delete
Per-user rate limiting on API surface
non_functional.description: Every authenticated endpoint rate-limited per-user via Bucket4j token buckets. Reads 600 req/min; writes 120 req/min; execute 60 req/min; send 10 req/min; bulk 20 req/min. 429 + Retry-After on exceeded. Redis-backed from M6 for cluster-wide accuracy.

constraints.title: Java 21 LTS (finalized language features only; preview disabled)
Spring Boot 3.3+ on Spring Framework 6.1+
Gradle 8+ with Kotlin DSL (wrapper committed)
Virtual threads enabled for request handling (spring.threads.virtual.enabled=true)
Virtual-thread task executor for @Async check execution
PostgreSQL 15+ in production (managed RDS)
Zonky Embedded PostgreSQL for local dev (no Docker, in-process, real Postgres 15 binary)
Spring Data JPA + Hibernate 6.4+; JSONB via @JdbcTypeCode(SqlTypes.JSON)
Flyway forward-only migrations under backend/src/main/resources/db/migration/
MapStruct for DTO ↔ entity conversion
Spring 6 RestClient (sync default) + WebClient (streaming) for HTTP integrations
Caffeine local cache for vertical slice; Redis (reactive) layered in when horizontally scaled
Spring @Scheduled for vertical slice; Quartz (JDBC-backed, cluster-safe) at M6
AWS SDK v2 for S3 object storage
JUnit 5 + AssertJ + Mockito + @SpringBootTest + @DataJpaTest
Testcontainers-PostgreSQL in CI; Zonky embedded in local
Code quality gates: Spotless (google-java-format) + Checkstyle + SpotBugs + JaCoCo
Vertical-slice package layout (bounded context per package, not layered-by-type)
CheckExecutor SPI — one implementation per CheckType
Database schema from ARCH §7 mirrored verbatim as Flyway V1 migration
JSONB configuration column for polymorphic check types
execution_results partitioned monthly by started_at
csi_metrics_current materialized view refresh strategy required
REST API base path /api/v1
Bearer JWT in Authorization header; 8-hour session with refresh token
Standard response envelope: { data, metadata: {total, page, limit, hasMore}, timestamp }
Containerized Eclipse Temurin 21 JRE; Spring Boot layered jar via bootBuildImage

assumptions_dependencies.title: Browser automation service (Selenium Grid or cloud equivalent) accessible
ITRS, Grafana, AppDynamics, Splunk APIs + credentials available
Citi System Inventory (CSI) API available, reliable, performant
Internal cloud platform provisions required infra (K8s, RDS, Redis, S3)
Enterprise OIDC issuer endpoint available with discoverable JWKS
Enterprise secrets vault with REST/gRPC client available

out_of_scope.title: New alerting engine replacing native tool alerting
New metrics or log collection system

user_stories_reference.summary: Create HTTP health check with CSI association
Investigate failed check with deep link
Create no-code UI test for login flow
Build cross-CSI EOD report with live preview and daily 6PM EST delivery

open_questions.question: What is the enterprise vault's client protocol (Vault OpenAPI / HashiCorp Vault / custom)?
Does ARCH §11 §Assumptions confirm the Browser Automation Service is Selenium Grid, or could it be Playwright Cloud?
open_questions.note: ARCH §4.4 M5 names 'Selenium Grid client' but §11 Assumptions says 'e.g., Selenium Grid or cloud-based service'

open_questions.question: Schema §7 defines 'tags' and 'secrets' tables but §8 retention policy does not cover their lifecycle. Required?
open_questions.note: Low priority — can default to no retention (indefinite)

open_questions.question: ARCH §12 does not document schedule CRUD endpoints explicitly. Are schedules managed inline with checks (PUT /checks/{id} with schedule payload) or via dedicated /schedules endpoints?
ARCH §7.1 execution_results partition table declares only execution_results_2024_01. What is the partition maintenance strategy (pg_partman? native? cron job?)?
